title: Advancing Complex Medical Communication in Arabic with Sporo AraSum: Surpassing Existing Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the model's ability to handle Arabic's complex morphology, syntax, and diglossia against models typically trained on Western languages. This is measured using quantitative NLP metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, BERTScore, F1) and human evaluation of 'Syntactic Proficiency' and 'Domain-Specific Linguistic Precision'.

Human evaluation of AI-generated clinical summaries using a modified PDQI-9 rubric, specifically scoring 'Cultural Competence' to assess whether the model understands and respects Arabic cultural, linguistic, and social nuances surrounding health beliefs and medical practices.

Human evaluation of clinical notes using the 'Free from Bias' attribute in a modified PDQI-9 rubric to verify that the generated text is strictly based on the patient-physician transcript and is not inappropriately influenced by the patient's characteristics.
